pages.title: A CAGE FOR GOD — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: 1. The creator of the system "ALL THAT EXISTS" cannot be OUTSIDE the system, because if he is not included in the system defined as "All That Exists", then he simply DOES NOT EXIST. 2. Nor can he be part of the system "ALL THAT EXISTS", alongside his creation, because a part is always simpler than the whole, and the creator cannot be simpler than the system he has created. 3. Only one way out remains: to identify the Creator with Creation: THE CREATOR IS ALL THAT EXISTS. Text supplied by the operator. pages.title: A HINT — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: If a photon from the Sun has been traveling for 7 minutes, it is not yet visible to an observer on Earth. It will become visible — in one minute. Therefore, the coordinate of this point is MINUS ONE. Do you understand what I'm getting at? Plus seven or minus one. Coordinates PLUS SEVEN or MINUS ONE. This is precisely what the RELATIVITY OF TIME is. Depending on the observer's location. (And the ninth minute for this event is once again minus one for the observer. Invisible again.) Continuing my reflections on the category of time: If movement from point A to point B occurs with an increase in magnitude, then movement from B to A must automatically ("by default") be characterized by a decrease in that magnitude. pages.title: The Anti-Universe — an Equal Partner of the Universe in the Cosmos — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: The most popular cosmological theory at present, the “Big Bang”, is not particularly satisfactory. No wonder the Pope himself praised it: it supposedly fits Church doctrine perfectly—there was nothing, and then God brought about that very “Bang!” That makes things simpler for the Pope. Scientists, however, are not all happy with it. For even if we allow for the existence of a Creator, the question immediately arises: what, then, is God himself, and where did he come from? So, for science, God is persona non grata. After the explosion, however, from the very first microseconds onward, apart from one small “but”, to which we shall return later, it is more or less clear how the Universe acquired its structure (S. Weinberg. The first three minutes, a modern view of the origin of the Universe, New York: Basic Books, 1993). On the whole, there is nothing supernatural about it: entropy increases overall, but, owing to the energy acquired at the moment of the “explosion”, a system displaced from equilibrium and developing nonlinearly (P. Covency and R. Highfield. The arrow of time, 1990) gives rise to self-organizing “subsystems”—from atoms and galaxies to living organisms, including thinking ones. And yet it remains unclear where that colossal energy of the “Big Bang” came from. It seems that things happen as follows: The Universe and the Anti-Universe exist eternally. This is not a “static” state, but their periodic appearance and disappearance—annihilation, “mutual destruction”—at moments corresponding to the “Big Bang” and/or the “Big Crunch”. A similar process is well known in quantum mechanics. S. Hawking, for example, writes that in so-called “empty space”, pairs of virtual particles and antiparticles continually appear and disappear: they arise together, move apart, and come together again to annihilate, releasing a certain amount of energy (S. Hawking. The illustrated a brief history of time, Bantam Books, 1997). “Since energy cannot be created out of nothing,” Hawking goes on to write, “one partner in a particle-antiparticle pair has positive energy and the other has negative energy.” Apparently, the same is true of the “Universe–Anti-Universe” system. It is precisely the force of attraction between these two worlds that gives rise to gravity, which opposes the expansion of the Universe that began with the “Big Bang”, “draws together” all its objects, and curves space and time, ultimately leading to the inevitable “Big Crunch” at the end of each cycle. Annihilation then once again supplies the colossal energy with which the Universe begins to develop in a new cycle—and so on “ad infinito”. Thus, of the three Friedmann models hitherto considered equally probable, Model I, that of a closed Universe, is the valid one; but the “Big Crunch” it predicts is not the end of everything, merely a new beginning. Let us return to quantum mechanics. There is a complex relationship between matter/antimatter, spatial symmetry, and the two directions of time. It consists in the following: if particles are replaced with antiparticles, spatial coordinates with their mirror images, and the direction of time is reversed—from the future to the past—the physical laws governing such an object remain unchanged (C, P, T-invariance) (P. Covency and R. Highfield. The arrow of time, 1990). Similar relationships apparently exist within the “Universe–Anti-Universe” pair: the Anti-Universe consists of antimatter (for a definition, see S. Weinberg. The first three minutes), has negative energy, is a “mirror image” of our Universe, and moves—develops, exists—backward in time, ensuring that all physical laws are preserved within the system. In the “singularity” prescribed by the “Big Bang” theory, by contrast, all laws break down. Indeed, the “total sum” of matter and energy in the “Universe–Anti-Universe” pair, as in a “particle-antiparticle” pair, remains unchanged and equal to zero. That is, in accordance with the first law of thermodynamics—the fundamental law of nature—energy and matter are neither created out of nothing nor lost. The system exists eternally and requires no Creator. As for the second law of thermodynamics, concerning the increase of entropy in the Universe, it too is, of course, valid—for the Universe, where irreversible processes occur, characterized by the positive direction of time, from the past to the future. “Irreversibility is the unidirectional development of a system with its inherent direction of time” (P. Covency and R. Highfield. The arrow of time, 1990). As is known, both classical and modern physical theories allow for both directions of time—the “law of time symmetry” (P. Covency and R. Highfield. The arrow of time, 1990). Entropy is a function of time: when time runs from the past to the future, entropy increases with time; when time “changes sign”, running from the future to the past, entropy correspondingly decreases. That is, in the Anti-Universe, which consists of antimatter and exists backward in time, entropy gradually decreases, thus maintaining the perfect symmetry of all parameters of the “Universe–Anti-Universe” pair at every moment. Thus, time, which according to Einstein can “slow down”, evidently “stops” at the moment of the “Big Bang”/“Big Crunch” and reverses its direction in the Anti-Universe. In other words, time, like the other coordinates, has two directions, extending both ways from zero. It is possible—and logical—that the curvature of space, too, upon reaching its maximum at the “singularity”, can acquire a “negative value” in the Anti-Universe, where space is, as it were, “turned inside out”, curving not like the surface of a sphere but like a “saddle surface”—or, more precisely, like the inner surface of a sphere, a “mirror image” of the configuration of the Universe. Interestingly, it is precisely such “saddle-shaped” curvature of space that, according to a number of authors, including S. Hawking, is required for travel “backward in time”. Here is a translation of Hawking’s limerick: “A lady nicknamed ‘Clever’ Wanted to travel down the street, But she was rushing Faster than light, And here was the penalty: The lady was back at her own front door, Long, alas, before setting off.” Since material objects cannot exceed the speed of light, such “effects” are apparently the prerogative of the Anti-Universe, its virtual particles, and the formations composed of them. Yet in the Universe, too, some very interesting phenomena occur at speeds close to the speed of light. As is known from quantum mechanics, a wave and a particle are two different descriptions of the same entity. The dual nature of particles is demonstrated in the so-called “double-slit experiment”: if light—electromagnetic waves—passes through two narrow slits in a barrier onto a detecting screen, interference fringes appear on it, as would be expected of wave processes. It was also discovered that if the light source is replaced with a source of particles, such as electrons, sent strictly one at a time, interference fringes again appear on the screen, although one would naturally expect each electron to pass through either one slit or the other. The interference pattern, however, indicates that the electron passes through both slits simultaneously! From this it was concluded that the electron is not only a particle but also a wave. What could explain such a phenomenon? As is known from “thought experiments”, at speeds exceeding the speed of light an object can “overtake itself” (“A lady nicknamed…”). Apparently, at speeds equal to the speed of light, one can “catch up with oneself”. “Any particle with zero rest mass,” writes S. Weinberg, “such as a photon, neutrino, or graviton, moves at the speed of light. Material particles approach the speed of light if their energy is to a considerable extent comparable to the rest energy mc², where m is the mass of the particle” (S. Weinberg. The first three minutes). Perhaps such a particle, moving at a speed close to that of light and “catching up with itself”, as it were “doubles”, being in “two places at once”, alongside itself. It thus acquires the ability to pass through both slits simultaneously, creating an interference pattern, for which it is accorded the “status” of a wave. As is known, wavelength is inversely proportional to the mass of the particle, which is quite logical, since particles of greater mass are harder to “accelerate” to the speed of light. The quantization of energy—that is, the fact that energy (electromagnetic waves—light, for example) is emitted not in a continuous stream but, as it were, in separate portions, “quanta”—is a natural consequence of the fact that a photon is first and foremost a particle, even though, having zero rest mass, it moves at the speed of light, where wave properties are most pronounced. And now, back to cosmology. The existence of the Anti-Universe does not seem so improbable if we recall the description of conditions in the primordial Universe, in the first moments after the “Big Bang”. “At first,” write I. Nicolson and P. Moore (I. Nicolson and P. Moore. The universe. Equinox, Oxford, 1985), “particles and antiparticles were constantly being created and mutually annihilated. Then … a tiny excess of particles over antiparticles arose—for reasons that are not yet entirely clear”—the very small “but” mentioned on the first page. To understand the reasons for this excess, let us turn once again to quantum mechanics. Quantum mechanics states that every particle has a partner—an antiparticle. This evidently refers to each “class of particles”. But if we take this statement more literally—that each individual particle has its own “partner”, an antiparticle, which is precisely what was happening at the beginning, in the “homogeneous soup” of the primordial Universe (see, for example, S. Weinberg; I. Nicolson and P. Moore)—we may suppose that if an excess of particles forms in the Universe, an equal excess of antiparticles must be accumulating somewhere. That is, when, as the temperature fell after the “Big Bang”, the Universe began to acquire structure and material particles combined into increasingly complex assemblies, antiparticles likewise conglomerated into antimatter, into the Anti-Universe. Such structuring—combining with “one’s own kind”—prevents the immediate annihilation of particles with antiparticles, postponing it for billions of years, from the “Big Bang” to the “Big Crunch”! On the basis of the above, it seems logical to conclude that the Universe—the sum of all particles—must inevitably have its partner: the sum of all antiparticles, the Anti-Universe. There is nothing “supernatural” about such an object, the “Anti-Universe”. The virtual particles of which it consists are, as is known, not picked up by detectors. But the existence of antiparticles is confirmed by their influence on material particles—a very noticeable influence indeed, extending to the annihilation of the latter. Likewise, the Anti-Universe—the cause of the future “Big Crunch”—is real because it has a determining influence on our Universe: its emergence, its development down to the smallest details, the motion of all its objects along geodesic baskets in the curved four-dimensional space-time continuum, its end, and the subsequent repetition of the cycle. There are rigid reciprocal connections between the Universe and the Anti-Universe. Because time runs in opposite directions in them, an event that is to occur in the Universe “tomorrow” has already occurred in the Anti-Universe “yesterday”, and vice versa. In other words, our world determines the past of the virtual world with the same inevitability with which the virtual world determines the future of ours. In this virtual, “imaginary” world, which exists backward in time, the use of imaginary numbers in calculations becomes justified. “Imaginary time is time measured using imaginary numbers” (S. Hawking, The illustrated a brief history of time). Mathematicians have long used imaginary numbers to solve cosmological problems—S. Hawking, R. Penrose, and others—but until now this method has been regarded as artificial, although S. Hawking notes: “Perhaps what we call imaginary time is actually more fundamental than real time” (S. Hawking, The illustrated a brief history of time). On the basis of the above, it would be more accurate to conclude that imaginary time is, at any rate, no less fundamental than real time. The world simply turns out to be more complex than we have imagined it until now—exactly “twice” as complex, by the addition of the Anti-Universe. It is then eternal, indestructible, self-contained, and requires no Creator, but merely repeats an endless cycle of states. Perhaps the Anti-Universe, where entropy decreases and, consequently, negentropy—in other words, information—increases (C. Shannon, I. Prigogine, L. Brillouin), may be regarded as an informational world. Some may find it tempting to call this informational, virtual world a “divine” substance, a kind of Higher Intelligence in which our future is supposedly determined. Well, that is a matter of taste. I would only point out that praying to such a God is useless: these reciprocal connections between the “world” and the “anti-world” are simply a consequence of the way the system exists, are governed by precise and immutable physical laws, and admit of no “appeal”. One may, of course, regret that our “free will” is, strictly speaking, merely an illusion in this world rigidly determined by cause-and-effect relationships. Yet because it is utterly impossible for us to predict coming events, this “illusion” should be taken quite seriously. For my part, I would simply repeat after Spinoza: “God is Nature.” There is no point in looking for anything outside it. Why, then, have the bodies of the Anti-Universe not yet been detected by scientists? Let us try to understand this question. It is known that on the cosmic scale, the concepts of space and time are inseparably linked: we measure the distance between celestial bodies by the time light needs to cover it. It is also known that a light wave spreading from a source travels both toward the observer—the forward light cone—and away from the observer—the reverse light cone. If we take the moment of an individual flash as the reference point, it is natural to regard the direction of photon motion in the forward cone as positive and that in the reverse cone as negative. Time undergoes corresponding changes: in the reverse cone, unlike the forward one, it takes on negative values, since each successive point lies further in the past than the preceding one—at a greater distance in light-years from the observer. That is, in the reverse cone, photons move backward in time, from the future to the past, on a negative time scale. Indeed, any object moving away from the observer can be regarded as moving backward in time: this is precisely why an astronaut’s time slows down. But will the astronaut enter negative time? Let us conduct a thought experiment. Suppose the astronaut’s speed is half the speed of light—in a thought experiment, anything is possible. Then, moving backward in time for, say, ten years, the astronaut covers a distance of five light-years, that is, goes five years into the past relative to Earth time, and must therefore set the clock back five years: 10 − 5 = 5. This means that the astronaut’s time has remained positive, although it has slowed by a factor of two. If, however, the astronaut’s speed is equal to the speed of light, then, travelling backward in time, the astronaut must set the clock back by exactly as many years as the journey has lasted: 10 − 10 = 0, that is, time has, as it were, stopped for the astronaut: at the end of the flight, the astronaut will be at the point where the vertices of the forward and reverse cones meet, at the epicentre of the wave. Finally, if the astronaut’s speed exceeds the speed of light—say, by a factor of two—the astronaut will enter the reverse light cone, negative time! The astronaut’s time is inverted and runs backward, since over ten years of travel the clock is set back twenty years: 10 − 20 = −10. Thus, the notion of unidirectional time apparently persists only because material objects cannot reach the speed of light, still less exceed it. Any object moving at a speed lower than that of light will sooner or later be overtaken by a light wave, which, after being reflected from it, will return to the observer. We can perceive only light travelling toward us, reaching the retina of the eye. Light from the reverse cone can be detected by the observer only if it is reflected from some object encountered along its path. It will then once again be a forward cone of light, but from a different source: as is known, all celestial bodies shine either by their own light or by reflected light and, in this sense, are independent sources of light for the observer. Is it surprising that, considering only light travelling in one direction, we also regard time as a unidirectional quantity? But does this mean that there are no objects in the cosmos capable of moving in negative time? Not at all. It means only that such objects cannot be detected by astronomers: since their speed exceeds the speed of light, a light wave will never catch up with them or be reflected from them, however long ago their motion began or however long it continues. The existence of such objects is confirmed only by indirect evidence (see above). There is, however, no doubt that the antiparticles formed in the primordial Universe cannot simply disappear. Their annihilation with their partners, material particles, proved impossible, since the latter still exist today in the objects of the material Universe. The antiparticles could only follow their example, group together, and form the bodies of the Anti-Universe. But whereas mass is a measure of inertia, antimatter objects apparently acquired the necessary mobility that allows them successfully to evade the close scrutiny of astronomers tirelessly searching for dark matter in the Universe. Objects moving at a speed exceeding the speed of light always remain in the reverse light cone and therefore cannot, in principle, be detected by an observer on Earth. It is precisely the totality of these objects that constitutes the Anti-Universe. It must be emphasized that, when dealing with objects of quantum mechanics, where the observer is, as it were, outside the system and can, under certain conditions, detect what happens in both the forward and reverse cones, particular care should be taken in classifying particles. Perhaps a clue may be found in whether or not the object has rest mass, as well as in properties such as the particle’s charge and spin. And finally, might photons, this boundary substance, be their own antiparticles precisely because they can visit both these worlds? 15 December 2000 Source: Samizdat. pages.title: The Celestial Clock Face — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Although the cosmos is an entire ocean of light from all kinds of sources, at any given moment Earth is washed by ONE SINGLE, quite specific wave: the light of a flash that occurred, say, 8 minutes ago at a distance of 8 light-minutes from Earth, or 5 hours ago at a distance of 5 light-hours, or a year ago at a distance of one light-year, or 40 years ago at a distance of 40 light-years, or a million (billion) years ago at a distance of a million (billion) light-years, and so on, all the way to the edge of the visible universe… The “crests” of this wave are segments of space and time, inseparably linked and “marked out” by the speed of light, where the distance in kilometres corresponds precisely to the time it takes light to cover that distance in a vacuum. This is the “celestial clock face”—the natural graduation of the cosmic scale, forming distinctive “time zones” of the universe. All other “events” are, at any given moment, entirely unobservable to a subluminal observer and therefore completely irrelevant, being in negative time—another, “not our own” dimension of cosmic space. For rays of the forward light cone, the scale is calibrated with successively increasing absolute values of the reading; in the reverse cone, with decreasing values. The point where the forward and reverse cones meet is the zero point of the scale. Naturally, when the zero point coincides with the observer’s location, the magnitude decreases in every direction of motion away from it. Source: Samizdat.

pages.title: Well, Would You Look at That! — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: In the cosmos, the only observable phenomena are “events”. An observer does not register “celestial bodies”, stars, planets, or assorted asteroids, but rather events. Because we Earthlings detect light — emitted or reflected (from primary or secondary sources, respectively) — from point sources (and in space all sources are point sources). And so far, Earthlings are the only known recipients. Light travels from an event (another flash, an emission of photons) to an observer. Along the shortest path, in a straight line. Distance is measured in light-travel time — the time photons need to cover that distance. And we always patiently wait for light from afar to reach the rods and cones of our retinas. As the Poet observed, even the light of stars long since dead reaches us sooner or later. For example, some fourteen billion years (give or take) have passed for us to see light from the farthest reaches of the observable universe. It's all very simple. But what is stranger, what is most incomprehensible, is how the sapiens who so proudly bear that name manage... to overlook the change in the sign of time when the direction of motion through space is reversed! Imagine that — in chorus (not boys, but learned grown men!) they proclaim a “positive arrow of time”! Whether our little seven-colored flower of light is flying from the event to the observer or the other way around. Yet if motion in one direction (toward us) is positive, motion in the opposite direction certainly is not! Negative time is the most natural, self-evident phenomenon, which scientists somehow manage (or prefer) not to see right in front of them. Not all of them, but the majority, along with the broad masses (who are ignorant, but may be forgiven). And there is nobody to set these sapiens straight: the crowning glory of creation. Scholars, they be! All that is required is to realize that if light travels from point A to point B, from the past into the present, then motion from B to A takes place in the opposite direction through space-time. Through the space-time continuum. In other words, when a cosmonaut sets off for distant stars, he flies into the past. “Let's go!” he shouts. “I want a second-class train ticket back to my childhood!” he yells. That is why the cosmonaut's time contracts each time, acquiring a “negative increment”. Because my eyesight has deteriorated, I cannot find a quotation from a book by Highfield and Coveney in which these specialists mention that, when we fly away into space, we are always moving into the past — at a modest speed, very different from the speed of light, but still... So take my word for it. Unlike the optics of my eyes, my brain's analytical apparatus is in excellent working order, regardless of what you may think about it. Russian original: Samlib.

pages.title: FIVE PRINCIPLES OF THE UNIVERSE — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: PRINCIPLE ONE The law of conservation, affirming the eternity, indestructibility and interconversion of matter and energy, encompasses all physical categories without exception: matter, antimatter and energy of all kinds and forms, including entropy as part of the positive energy of the system and negentropy, i.e. information, which, according to Shannon, is entropy with the opposite sign. PRINCIPLE TWO Cosmic objects consisting of antimatter are in principle invisible to us because, having a speed greater than that of light, they are always in the reverse light cone relative to the observer (in negative time), but their existence is confirmed by indirect evidence — their undeniable influence on the bodies of the material Universe, which is what makes astrophysicists search for the notorious "dark matter". PRINCIPLE THREE The Big Bang is nothing other than the annihilation of all the matter (mass) existing in the world with all the antimatter contained in it. From the energy of the explosion, the development of antipodal worlds begins again, until their next annihilation. This process is cyclical and eternal, like that for a "particle-antiparticle" pair. PRINCIPLE FOUR Whether a quantum-mechanical object is a particle or a wave depends exclusively on the speed of that object: at subluminal speeds it is a particle; at the speed of light or at speeds close to it, it is a wave. Upon reaching a superluminal speed, the object manifests itself as an antiparticle — with corresponding changes in all other parameters. PRINCIPLE FIVE Time, like spatial dimensions, has two directions along the coordinate axis — in both directions from zero—that is, from the flash (“event”): positive time in the forward light cone and negative time in the reverse one. The movement of any object towards the observer is always the positive direction of movement, and away from the observer is the negative direction, both in space and in time.

pages.title: The Formula of Everything and Other Nice Things — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Recognizing the existence of negative time makes it possible: to discard the need for any external, supernatural force (a Creator) for the emergence of the Universe. to propose a reliable FORMULA OF EVERYTHING: E - E = E + i^2E (i squared multiplied by E) E = mc^2, if anyone remembers; to explain: the nature of the Big Bang, quantum-wave dualism, the cause of the curvature of space, the operating principle of the Universe - a unique Perpetual Motion Machine, the meaning of the category of time, the Twin Paradox, the preferability of Friedmann’s First Model, the mathematical Formula of Everything, the inevitability of superluminal velocities, the existence of a CPT-symmetric world, the tachyonic mass of antiparticles, the violation of cause-and-effect relationships in the “looking-glass world,” the complementarity of entropy and information, -the eternity of these physical concepts, the existence of a certain single fundamental essence undergoing a ‘phase transition’ depending on velocity, the nature of gravity (and electricity), the composition of dark matter and energy, and all that sort of thing, including...“the difficult character of the Lord God Almighty.”

pages.title: God and Systems Theory — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: The creator of everything that exists cannot be outside the system, for then he... does not exist (that which is outside what exists does not exist). Nor can he be included among everything that exists alongside the other components, because then he is part of the system, and a part is always simpler than the whole. At the same time, systems theory implies that the creator of a system cannot be simpler than the system he has created. The conclusion (the only possible one) is that the Creator must be identified with the Creation: God is the world. Note: our knowledge of the world is far from perfect. Do not get fixated.

pages.title: The Lemniscate — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Acknowledging the existence of a CPT-symmetric Anti-World makes it possible to: dispense with the need for any external, supernatural force (a Creator) to bring the Universe into being. find an explanation for how the Universe can arise from nothing without violating physical laws. show the possibility of an eternal world. understand where the energy of the Big Bang came from. explain the nature of gravity. justify a preference for Friedmann’s first model (until now, all three have been regarded as equally probable). explain the emergence of an apparent “excess of particles” over antiparticles in the primordial Universe. establish the cause of the curvature of space and time postulated by Einstein. justify the use of imaginary (and complex) numbers in cosmological calculations. complete the time scale so that time, like the other—spatial—coordinates, has two directions, extending both ways from zero. resolve the paradox of irreversibility, whereby microprocesses (quantum-mechanical ones) appear reversible, while macroprocesses do not. explain the dual nature of particles (their wave properties). And finally, as regards predicting possible outcomes of possible experiments: suggest that, when light is slowed down (the latest achievement of experimental physics), the photon in all likelihood loses its wave properties. (To test this, the double-slit experiment must be repeated in an apparatus that slows down light). P.S. The much-discussed “Quantum Entanglement” amply confirms the acquisition of wave properties upon reaching relativistic speeds. Source: Samizdat.

pages.title: SCHRØDINGER CAT'S MEMO — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: "The observer sees the light (emitted or reflected) only at the moment when photons have reached his retina, the light-sensitive part of his vision system. As any light emission takes place before it is seen, the photons always travel towards the observer from past to future. This is considered as a normal, positive flow of time. Photons and other object, travelling away from observer, move back in time, that is, from future to the past. Therefore, time has a negative increment in this case. Herewith, the time of objects moving slower than the speed of light, slows down, remaining positive. At the speed of light, the negative gain of time is so great that time stops, and the moving object acquires wave characteristics, i.e. the property to be observed in many places simultaneously. Objects travelling faster than the speed of light, got in a real negative time, where the entropy and cause-and-effect relationship are reversed. Cosmic objects, existing in negative time, are inaccessible for visual control of the observer. However, these objects are as real as any other objects. It is antimatter that 'hides' in the negative time; it annihilates with all matter of the Universe at the moment of each next 'Big Bang'. Summarizing the above: It is indeed a dreadful crime Not to admit the backward time."

pages.title: Meow — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: I have done my part — I have discovered a new physical reality, one that requires a new mathematical framework. Incidentally, I have proposed the final formula myself: it is simple, as a “Formula of Everything” ought to be. pages.title: Monitoring Time in Space — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: “The use of the term ‘space-time’ stems from a poverty of terminology. We might just as well call water ‘hydrogen–oxygen’” (M. Kamenarovich). “Where nothing happens, there is no time. For time is not a quantity introduced into a system from outside, but an immanent property of the world, connected with the nature of the changes taking place within it. There may be several times moving in different directions. Some are reversible, others are not. From the observer’s point of view… only one time flows, of course; this happens because the observer measures time by their own clock, because they have immersed all the diverse streams of time in the single time given to them by Nature” (Stanisław Lem). All classical scientific theories claimed to describe the world objectively, but did not take into account the observer’s influence on the object of knowledge. The new physics is called upon to abandon this underestimation of the observer’s role without denying the possibility of obtaining objective knowledge. Both relativity and quantum mechanics have emphatically demonstrated the need for such an approach. To retain objectivity, we must clearly establish the circumstances in which the observer assesses incoming information, understand the reasons for the involuntary limitations of our assessment, and foresee their consequences. For example, an observer can see only emitted or reflected light, at the moment photons reach the receptors of their eye (auxiliary optics do not alter the principle). Photons need some time to reach the observer, so any emission of particles occurs before it is detected. That is, photons move from the “event” to the observer in ordinary positive time—from the past to the future. It is precisely positive time that today’s official science, with the exception of a few outstanding scientists, regards as the only real time. Nevertheless, let us try to examine the situation more deeply. Clearly, if the emission of photons is taken as the initial, zero moment of time, then, as the particles move toward the observer, their time coordinates will take on positive values of increasing magnitude. But if, conversely, the reference point (“time zero”) is associated with the observer’s location, it is logical to conclude that time must take on negative values whose magnitude is greater the farther the moving point is from the observer in space. One can, of course, also measure from any “nonzero” point, bearing in mind that motion away from the observer always takes place in “reverse” time, from the future to the past. Backward motion in time can occur either with a decrease in the magnitude of positive numbers or with an increase in the magnitude of negative numbers, depending on the coordinates of the starting point. When moving from the event to the observer, however, as already indicated above, the changes correspond, conversely, to an increase in the magnitude of positive values or a decrease in the magnitude of negative ones. Moreover, this applies to any subluminal observer, wherever they may be, which supports both the isotropy of the universe and the objective nature of the knowledge obtained. The speed of motion plays only an auxiliary role, in the sense that the decrease or increase in the absolute values of time readings occurs more rapidly at a higher speed. When the observed object moves at a subluminal speed, a negative increment in magnitude makes it possible to register only a compression, a slowing of time, which nevertheless retains positive values. The unobservability of the reverse motion of photons (away from the recipient) and, consequently, the “elusiveness” of genuine negative time have given grounds for speaking of a supposedly unidirectional “arrow of time” in the Universe, since our world of positive mass is a world of subluminal speeds. But already at the speed of light (characteristic of energy-carrying particles), the negative increment “cancels out” the entire course of positive time. The time of photons and other particles travelling at the speed of light is zeroed out. The particle acquires wave properties and, as it were, is “multiplied” into several places at once, providing a logical explanation of the quantum–wave duality of particles. Superluminal objects, however, which are inaccessible to visual observation, acquire a kind of “overshoot” of reverse time thanks to their speed beyond the limit. As a result, they are constantly in genuine NEGATIVE (“minus”) time, regardless of their direction of motion. Figuratively speaking, the superluminal “traveller” becomes not only “younger than their brother”, but younger than their own self, entering their own past. The world of superluminal speeds is a world of “cosmic invisibles”, a world of inverted cause-and-effect relationships. In quantum mechanics, antiparticles exist in reverse (negative) time (the rule of CPT symmetry). The “dark matter” of the Universe apparently consists of antimatter as well. That is, if antimatter has “disappeared”, it has done so only from our field of view, which makes any talk of a violation of the law of conservation entirely meaningless. Human beings cannot perceive the “symmetrical” world through their senses, but this by no means implies that such a world is unreal: indirect evidence and the logic of things unequivocally support its existence. It should also be understood that the concept of negative time does not refute relativity, but develops and improves it. Relativity becomes a special case of a new generalized theory that makes it possible to resolve many of the unsolved problems of modern physical science—the very problems whose solutions have long been “in the air”. Source: Samizdat.

pages.title: MOVEMENT — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Movement away from an observer means only that an object is moving with a “negative increment” of time. For a “cosmonaut” traveling at subluminal speed, time WILL REMAIN POSITIVE, but it will SLOW DOWN (a well-known phenomenon). The cosmonaut will “grow younger”)). IF the cosmonaut could, while moving away, attain the SPEED OF LIGHT (but being MATERIAL, with positive rest mass, he cannot: mass is a measure of inertia), then his time WOULD stop. For tiny particles, however, this is possible. Upon reaching the speed of light, they turn into a wave, “double” (the double-slit experiment). Time coming to a halt means that the object IS IN TWO PLACES AT ONCE (the difference between a wave and a particle, which occupies a definite place at a definite moment in time). But only when the object's speed becomes FASTER THAN LIGHT DOES TIME BECOME DISTORTED, beginning to flow from the future into the past. IT BECOMES NEGATIVE. And it is precisely in negative time that ANTIMATTER lives (in accordance with the principle of CPT symmetry, well known to all the physicists in Geneva who have studied antihydrogen). pages.title: Multiplicity of Worlds — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: As is known, virtual “particle - antiparticle” pairs continually appear in a vacuum. Such a pair is, in fact, the only system reliably known to modern science that exists eternally. (!) Imagine for a minute that inside such a pair there live... thinking beings. Do not be embarrassed; after all, there is no limit to fantasy. So then. For such “intellectuals,” living, for example, inside some structure belonging to the PARTICLE, would it matter that there are a great many such pairs in... our Universe? I assure you - not in the slightest! Here the principle called “Occam’s Razor” should be applied: “Do not create unnecessary complexities without urgent need.” Our hypothetical beings are absolutely indifferent not only to the fact that there are many such pairs, but also to the fact that all of them are included in some superset that is our Universe: their WORLD, their GOD is ONE AND ONLY for them. Tiny “thinkers” have no concern for our Universe: the maximum it makes sense for them to discuss is the origins and possible death of their own world, that is, the problems of formation and development of precisely this pair of antipodes, the only one important to them. Now let us move on to considering the Universe. If it too has its cosmic partner, its antipode - an anti-universe, and this pair is an eternal, self-sufficient system that requires no external “supernatural” force for its emergence and existence (development), does it matter to us whether only one such pair exists at all, or whether, for example, it is included, alongside others like it, in, say, some “hyper-universe”? Absolutely not! Just as “the vassal of my vassal is not my vassal,” so too “the God of my God is not my God.” For us, ALL THAT EXISTS is precisely OUR WORLD, OUR GOD. Occam’s Razor. Do you understand? Here the main thing is not the number of sets at all, but ONLY THE PRINCIPLE: THE LAW OF ANTIPODES, without which a system cannot be complete and self-sufficient, cannot claim the role of an eternal and infinite - divine - essence. EVERYTHING THAT EXISTS for us is an eternal pair, cyclically appearing and disappearing at the moment of annihilation (“Big Bang/Big Crunch”): the Universe plus the Anti-Universe. This is our dual WORLD, this is our only GOD. .......... but - one can also go on pouring from empty into void, if someone is fascinated by that activity.

pages.title: Once More on the Evolution of the Universe — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: The most popular cosmological theory at present, the “Big Bang”, is not entirely satisfactory. The Pope praised it for being fully consistent with Church doctrine: there was nothing, and then God brought about that very “Big Bang”. But for a true scientist, God is “persona non grata” in the sense that, even if the existence of a Creator is accepted, science immediately faces the question of what this God actually is and where he came from. In other words, the concept of God as an unknowable entity is a dead end for science. Nevertheless, the “Big Bang” theory cannot answer the question of where this colossal energy ultimately came from. After the Bang, however, literally from the very first milliseconds, it is more or less clear how the Universe acquired its structure. There is nothing supernatural about it: entropy increases overall, but owing to the energy acquired at the moment of the explosion, the system departs from equilibrium and, developing nonlinearly, gives rise to self-organizing “subsystems”—from atoms and galaxies to living organisms, including thinking ones. Yet the very beginning can be explained only as follows: the Universe and the Anti-Universe exist eternally in the world. This is not a static state, but their periodic emergence, development, and disappearance at moments corresponding to the “Big Bang/Big Crunch”. Quantum mechanics describes a similar process of the continual appearance and disappearance (annihilation) of virtual “particle-antiparticle” pairs. Since energy cannot be created out of nothing, one partner has positive energy and the other negative energy, Hawking notes. The same is true of the “Universe–Anti-Universe” system. It is precisely the force of attraction between these two worlds that gives rise to gravity, which “draws together” all objects and curves space and time, ultimately leading to the inevitable “Big Crunch” at the end of each cycle, in accordance with Friedmann’s first model. But this is not the end of everything, merely a new beginning, since the energy of annihilation once again allows the Universe—and the Anti-Universe—to develop in a new cycle, and so on “ad infinito”. Perhaps such an idea, “lying on the surface”, has occurred to scientists more than once and been dismissed for the simple reason that the presence of antimatter objects in the cosmos has never been confirmed by astronomers. Antiparticles, meanwhile, are exclusively the province of quantum mechanics. What is the reason for this state of affairs? I would like to remind the reader that we can observe only celestial bodies that either emit their own light or reflect light. Suppose, however, that some cosmic object moves faster than light. In that case, a light wave cannot catch up with it and therefore cannot be reflected from it. Such an object cannot, in principle, be detected by astronomers: it will always be in the “reverse cone” of light. It is known that a material body cannot reach the speed of light, still less exceed it. But as for the category of antimatter… why not? After all, if mass is a measure of inertia, perhaps “antimass” has precisely the opposite properties and is a kind of “measure of mobility”? When studying objects of quantum mechanics, however, the researcher is, as it were, “outside the system” and can sometimes also “peek” into the reverse light cone. Might this explain a property such as particle spin, whereby a particle looks different in different directions (rather like… the phases of the Moon)? Quantum mechanics tells us that there is a special relationship between matter and antimatter, spatial symmetry, and the two directions of time. It consists in the following: if particles are replaced with antiparticles, spatial coordinates with their mirror images, and the direction of time is reversed—from the future to the past—the physical laws governing such an object remain unchanged. Similar relationships apparently exist within the “Universe–Anti-Universe” pair: the Anti-Universe consists of antimatter, has negative energy, is a “mirror image” of our Universe, and exists backward in time, ensuring that all physical laws are preserved within the system. The total sum of matter and energy remains unchanged and equal to zero, in accordance with the first law of thermodynamics. The second law of thermodynamics, concerning increasing entropy, is also, of course, valid—for the material Universe, where irreversible processes occur, characterized by the positive direction of time, from the past to the future. In the Anti-Universe, however, where time runs backward, entropy, being a function of time, gradually decreases, thus maintaining the perfect symmetry—and stability—of all the system’s parameters at every moment. Thus, time, which stops at the moment of the “Big Bang”, has two directions as one moves away from that moment, extending both ways from zero, like spatial coordinates: time is positive in the Universe and negative in the Anti-Universe. The curvature of space acquires a “negative” value in the Anti-Universe, where space is, as it were, “turned inside out”, curving not like the surface of a sphere but like a saddle surface—or, if you prefer, like the inner surface of a sphere, a mirror image of the configuration of the Universe. Interestingly, it is precisely such “saddle-shaped” curvature of space that, according to a number of authors, is required for travel backward in time. Only objects moving faster than light travel into the past—that is, when an object can “overtake itself”. By contrast, objects capable of reaching the speed of light, or a speed close to it, can “catch up with themselves”. For them, time, as it were, stops; they “double”, acquiring the ability to be in two places at once. This is precisely what happens to particles in the double-slit experiment when they begin to exhibit wave properties. Acknowledging the existence of the Anti-Universe makes it possible to resolve virtually all the unsolved questions of modern cosmology, in particular to locate the “disappeared” antiparticles, which evidently never disappeared at all (indeed, that would contradict the first law of thermodynamics). They merely combined with their own kind into increasingly complex assemblies, following the example of their material partners, and, acquiring the corresponding speed, vanished… from our field of view. In conclusion, I would also like to note that the entropy of the Anti-Universe, like its energy in general, apparently has a negative sign. This is that very “negentropy”, or, equivalently, information according to Shannon. What, then? Cosmic fields of information? A Higher Intelligence, perhaps? The indestructibility of our consciousness, which is nothing other than the totality of our knowledge about ourselves and the world around us—in other words, information? Perhaps the immortality of our soul? I do not know. I would only repeat after Spinoza: “God is Nature.” There is no point in looking for anything outside it. Source: Samizdat.

pages.title: A Paradigm for a Pair of “Diggers” — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Physicists have long been interested in where the antiparticles formed in the primordial universe in accordance with the law of conservation could have gone. Annihilation did not take place, as the very existence of the material world demonstrates. There can therefore be only one satisfactory answer to this question: if they have “disappeared”, they have disappeared solely from our field of view, and nowhere else. In fact, cosmic invisibles made of supposedly “lost” antimatter—antipodal copies of familiar celestial bodies—are still alive and well today, in reverse, negative time, inaccessible to us. What is negative time? A person sees only light that has reached the retina of their eye. Any flash of light always occurs before it is seen, since photons need a certain amount of time to reach the observer. Thus, photons and indeed all objects approaching the observer move “from earlier to later”, from the past to the future—that is, in ordinary, forward-flowing, positive time. It is logical to conclude that objects (photons and others) moving away from the observer, conversely, move in reverse, “backward” in time. For example, at any given moment, the farther a celestial body is from Earth, the deeper in the past it is relative to the observer. Our eyes cannot detect receding photons that do not reach the retina. However, any object that finds itself in a stream of photons may be able to reflect these receding photons and redirect them toward the observer, albeit with a delay relative to the initial flash. Then we will see these photons, but now reflected, with a certain delay indicating the negative increment that has occurred in their motion through time. If the object’s speed is subluminal, the photons will catch up with it fairly soon, and time, having slowed somewhat, will remain positive. The object will become a source of reflected light and will be detected as such by the observer. If the speed of motion equals the speed of light, the negative increment cancels out the entire positive course of time. Time is “zeroed out”, stops, demonstrating the object’s wave properties—its ability to be in many places simultaneously (all “massless”, energy-carrying particles have precisely this speed). Finally, for an object moving faster than light, time is completely inverted: it begins to run from the future to the past, taking on NEGATIVE values. Objects in genuinely negative time are entirely inaccessible to visual observation: travelling at superluminal speeds, they cannot, in principle, be overtaken by photons (regardless of their direction of motion), produce no reflected light, and remain forever invisible to us. There is no point even trying to “see” the dark matter of the universe. Only indirect evidence will indicate its undoubted presence. Evidently, this is precisely the “disappeared” antimatter. The conclusion is supported by quantum mechanics: antimatter exists in negative time (the rule of CPT symmetry). Inverted time corresponds to the complete reversibility of entropic processes, which is precisely what ensures the eternal existence of the physical world, turning it into a Cosmic Perpetual-Motion Machine—a cyclic process of the formation, development, and involution of antipodal worlds, from one annihilation Big Bang to the next—“ad infinito”. If, in a scientific debate, you are armed only with facts and logic, your concept will be rejected. Unless two or three “diggers” who happen to read it dig down to the heart of the matter. You can dig, or you can choose not to. Up to you. Source: Samizdat.

pages.title: The Principle of Causality — a Reason to Stand on Principle — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: There is no doubt that acknowledging the existence, alongside the material universe, of a world made of antimatter, with time running backward, is in itself tantamount to acknowledging that a signal can propagate faster than light. Many mistakenly believe that the Theory of Relativity prohibits superluminal speeds. This is entirely untrue. The prohibition on motion faster than light comes neither from special relativity nor from the mathematical calculations of Maxwell or Lorentz, but solely from… the principle of causality. Einstein himself, considering the question of superluminal signal transmission, wrote: “WE ARE COMPELLED TO CONSIDER POSSIBLE A MECHANISM OF SIGNAL TRANSMISSION IN WHICH THE RESULTING EFFECT PRECEDES ITS CAUSE.” And further: “Although this result contains no logical contradictions, it nevertheless conflicts so strongly with the character of all our experience that the impossibility of the assumption V > C appears sufficiently justified.” Notice that after the word “although”, the discussion concerns nothing more than everyday experience, which once provided the basis for notions of a flat Earth and has no direct bearing on science in general or relativity in particular. That is, it is rather this very statement by Einstein that contradicts special relativity, whereas the theory itself, on the contrary, “compels” us to acknowledge the possibility of superluminal speeds. Yet the notion that a superluminal signal speed supposedly contradicts relativity has become so deeply rooted that even L. Wong, who conducted an impressive experiment in which the speed of light was exceeded by a factor of 300(!) under laboratory conditions, believes that this experiment… is inconsistent with relativity! At the same time, the scientist reasonably emphasizes that the claim that superluminal speeds are unattainable apparently applies only to objects with a rest mass greater than zero. “Light, however, can be represented either as waves, to which the concept of mass does not apply at all, or as photons with a rest mass known to be zero,” Wong writes, “so the speed of light in a vacuum is by no means the limit.” Let us note in passing that, strictly speaking, a photon is never “at rest” at all. So, we need to separate the issues here. First of all, we must understand that the principle of causality, which breaks down at and above the speed of light, has a domain of applicability confined to the world of matter. It does not apply to the field—energy-carrying particles—since massless particles, upon reaching the speed of light, can be in many places at once, in accordance with wave properties, and can serve as their own antiparticles. Still less can it apply to objects made of antimatter, which invariably exist in reversed time, where entropy, a function of time, does not increase as it does in the world of matter, but decreases. Consequently, processes are reversible, and it is precisely this reversibility that allows an effect to precede its cause! So, let me repeat: the principle of causality is unshakable for the material (visible) universe. But the world of antimatter is precisely the environment that allows superluminal speeds to become a physical reality. In the words of antihydrogen researchers, it is “a key to another universe, where time reverses its direction—from the future to the past—everything left becomes right, and everything positive becomes negative”. Indeed, one need only know that the masses of a particle and an antiparticle can annihilate each other to understand that these masses differ fundamentally in some respect. And at least at the moment of annihilation, they can hardly have the same sign. Otherwise, they would add together rather than cancel each other out. It seems that nature contains a single fundamental entity that changes so profoundly with its speed of motion that it takes on different signs—from positive, through zero, to imaginary and negative values (alternatively, the square of an imaginary quantity)—penetrating another space-time dimension. Since we, inhabitants of an exclusively material world, have only a positive “measuring stick”, we are inclined to declare it “ordinary positive mass” if and when we contrive to capture and measure it, thereby violating the rule of CPT symmetry, as a result of which… the first law of thermodynamics appears to be violated(!). And we like to repeat that the antiparticle’s “ordinary positive mass” is an “established fact”. Yet even a particle’s mass at rest is an elastic concept, since, strictly speaking, a particle, too, does not exist at rest. As Einstein wittily remarked, if a fact contradicts the theory, so much the worse for the fact. Still, anyone can make a mistake in the finer points of interpretation by yielding to the weight of conventional wisdom. What matters is that the scientific method allows people to perceive the world around them as accurately as possible and to correct their mistakes as new knowledge accumulates. Today, when even the latest radio-wave studies by astrophysicists give grounds for suspecting that certain cosmic objects move at superluminal speeds, and an impressive number of experiments both slowing down and speeding up light have been conducted in laboratories around the world, we can be confident that Einstein, with his remarkable ability to think unconventionally, would no longer make such a sweeping statement about the inadmissibility of superluminal speeds, which his own theory “compels us to discuss”. As for those who take an excessively principled stand on preserving the inviolability of outdated postulates, without understanding the essence of relativity, and wish to be more Catholic than the Pope… well, we must admit that they are no Einsteins. Unfortunately. Source: Samizdat.

pages.title: Quiver of Time Arrows — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Whenever one comes across profound reflections on the “mysterious and incomprehensible” nature of time, one always wants to object: but there is... no mysticism here, gentlemen! The universal measure of space and time in the Universe is the speed of light. In a vacuum it is constant and equals 300,000 kilometers per second. That is, a second is simply the time during which light manages to cover 300 thousand kilometers. The photons have flown 300,000 km, which means a second has passed. Accordingly, a minute is a span of time during which photons cover a distance 60 times greater, 18,000,000 km. To express an hour in kilometers, multiply by sixty once again. Want to know what a year is? Please! An astronomical year is the time during which light travels about 9.5 trillion kilometers. Half a year, therefore, is 9.5 trillion km divided by two. A month is one twelfth of the same figure, and so on. 14 billion years, the postulated age of the universe, is approximately ten to the twenty-third power kilometers, which also means the size (radius) of the visible Universe. To generalize: time is the distance that light covers during that time. In other words, any time can be expressed in kilometers. An important consequence follows: if a quantity is expressed in units of length, then it is a vector and can assume both positive and negative values. Incomprehensibly, people still argue about the existence of negative time. How did it happen that negative time was “overlooked”? The thing is that an observer, wherever he may be, sees only the light caught by the receptors of his organ of vision, the light that comes into contact with them. Receding photons are not registered by the observer, except in those cases when, and if, on the way they catch up with some object and reflect from it, in order to return to the observer once more, albeit with a delay. Auxiliary optics do not change the principle; that is, the emitting or reflecting (secondary) source is registered, but always only the light that has reached the observer. Since any flash occurs earlier than it is seen, the motion of photons toward the observer is directed from the past into the future. And motion from the past into the future is precisely the normal, positive flow of time. Conversely, the motion of photons in the opposite direction, away from the observer, proceeds backward in time, from the future into the past. This is the negative course of time, when each subsequent point lies deeper in the past than the previous one. The movement of photons (and other objects) in any direction from the point where the observer himself is located is always directed away from him. From any other point in the universe (the so-called “events”), direction is possible either toward the observer, into the future (the direct light cone), or away from him, into the past (the reverse light cone). The motion of photons backward, away from the observer, wherever it may begin, necessarily provides a negative increment of time, while the magnitude of this increment depends on the speed of objects moving within the photon streams that are potentially capable of reflecting those photons and once again “redirecting” them to the observer. If an object possesses a subluminal velocity, sooner or later it will be overtaken by a light wave and turned into a source of reflected light, that is, it will be detected in positive time. Thus ordinary celestial bodies, initially located in the reverse light cone of some flash, will later inevitably be registered by the observer, albeit with a certain delay. Whether an astronaut notes the slowing of time, whether the cosmic traveler grows younger in the “twin paradox” while moving away from Earth, they too always remain in the positive time familiar to us, despite a certain negative increment. Positive time is our world, our reality, our dimension, because all objects of the material world (substantial, with positive mass), including the observer, move at subluminal velocities. The upper, unattainable limit for them is the speed of light. Photons possess such a speed, the visible part of electromagnetic radiation, and in general all “massless,” energy-bearing particles. When a particle develops the speed of light, the negative increment of its time exactly corresponds in magnitude to the positive time that has elapsed since the beginning of motion. If a microscopic astronaut were placed inside a photon, he would have to turn his clock hands backward along the way, making sure that the hands constantly remained in their initial position. The resultant for such an object is “time zero.” The particle both starts and reaches its goal simultaneously, in one and the same instant of “stopped” time. It as though “catches up with itself,” “doubles itself” (recall the “double-slit” experiment). An object possessing the speed of light gains the ability to be in several places at once, that is, it acquires the properties of a wave. A wave differs from a particle precisely in that it is observed not in one definite place at a definite moment, but in many places synchronously. Incidentally, the ability of photons to be in positive and negative time simultaneously underlies their capacity to serve as “antiparticles to themselves.” And finally, if an object exceeds the speed of light, then the negative increment of time will be so great that its time will be utterly perverted, will become truly negative, will acquire a minus sign with the accompanying inversion of cause-and-effect relations: it will “reach its destination at seven in the morning yesterday.” Since formations possessing superluminal velocity traverse any segment of space faster than photons do, they always outpace the corresponding light wave, even when moving toward the observer. In such a case the unavoidable excess of the path they have traversed, in comparison with the rays, will already be directed away from the observer, which means, once again, negative time. Thus objects exceeding the speed of light exist in negative time constantly, regardless of the direction of their motion. They are not overtaken by light, are incapable of reflecting it, and cannot become “secondary” sources of light. Therefore negative time is a world invisible to the subluminal observer, another dimension, another reality. What, then, are the essences that inhabit this reality? Quantum mechanics tells us that antiparticles live in negative time. Their characteristic spin indicates precisely their being in the reverse light cone, which is not shared with the observer. It is logical to suppose that on cosmic scales there also exist formations of antimatter that possess superluminal velocity and for that reason remain in negative time, invisible to us. Indirect signs of their existence, apparently, are what compel scientists to speak of the notorious “black holes,” which absorb (more accurately, do not reflect!) even light, or of some mysterious “dark matter.” The existence of such phenomena is only a hypothesis, like the “tachyon,” a hypothetical micro-object of negative time. But if superluminal cosmic invisibles are possible, then why assign something purely speculative to that role? After all, quite real antimatter has “disappeared,” been “lost,” and in fact there ought to be no less of it in the universe than ordinary mass, since, in accordance with the law of conservation, pairs of antipodal particles appeared precisely as pairs. They also could have disappeared only in pairs. And if ordinary particles continue to exist to this day in material objects, the same should be expected of their analogous antipodes. Formations made of antiparticles are “non-material” structures, antimatter, the anti-matter invisible to us. Incidentally, it is quite possible that there is even more of such a virtual, imaginary substance in space than of material objects, since for mutual annihilation with a positive unit what is required is not merely an imaginary unit, but its square, capable at a certain moment of providing the “minus one” of mass required for annihilation. It seems that “tachyons,” “black holes,” and other “mysterious invisibles” are simply states of objects made of antimatter, corresponding to their being in the natural environment of their existence, in negative time. As is known, the transfer of antimatter into our time for the purpose of “observing and measuring” is carried out by... cooling superluminal formations almost to absolute zero (one of the ways of slowing particles). Is it worth being surprised that the parameters of the object turn out to differ from the expected ones? The fact that we cannot directly observe, but can only comprehend an imaginary, “tachyonic” mass is entirely in the order of things, for the mass of “fast” particles depends on their speed. The experiment, as it should, affects its own result. And the quantity of changes may, perhaps, turn into quality: a particle may become a wave, even an antiparticle, and vice versa, depending on the speed of motion. One single fundamental essence in its different “hypostases.” The conclusion suggests itself that all discrepancies in the interpretation of classical theories and quantum mechanics arise simply because it is difficult for the researcher to interpret macro-processes in strict accordance with those of quantum objects, since on the cosmic scale he himself is inside, not outside, the system, and besides is incapable of acting upon macro-world objects. Taking the above considerations into account could help in resolving many long-ripened contradictions and problems of physics, in particular in understanding the nature of the Big Bang, which, it seems, is nothing other than yet another annihilation of all the matter present in the universe with all its antimatter. This annihilative explosion is fully capable of supplying that colossal energy from which the formation of antipodal worlds begins anew in the endless cycle of the transformation of matter into radiation and back again. Exactly so, by analogy with the only eternal system reliably known to modern official science, the pair “particle antiparticle” in a vacuum, the physical world that obeys the law of conservation is, by the logic of things, arranged as a unique and all-encompassing Cosmic Perpetual Motion Machine.

pages.text: only a cyclic process is eternal, one that is inherently reversible. two antipodes—the manifest and the imaginary— the world of the Absolute, a wonder without wonders, where relative time and space ensure the constancy of all categories. pages.title: A Simple Solution to the Twin Paradox — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: The rejection, contrary to the logic of the theory of relativity, of superluminal velocities (and thereby of negative time) led to the notion that, after making a loop through outer space and returning to Earth, the traveler twin would turn out to be younger than his stay-at-home brother. A paradox that is still considered unresolved to this day. Yet recognizing the reality of negative time solves this paradox very simply. What, then, is time that flows backward, from the future into the past? A person registers photons only at the moment they strike the retina. Any emission of photons always occurs before it is seen, because photons need a certain amount of time to reach the observer. Therefore, the motion of photons, and of all objects in general that approach the observer, takes place “from earlier to later,” from the past into the future, in ordinary positive time, with its absolute values increasing. Accordingly, movement away from the observer means motion backward, from the future into the past, going ever deeper as the distance from the recipient increases. That is, by changing direction in space, the traveler also changes the direction of motion in time. Therefore, during a “there-and-back” journey, the difference between the readings of the traveler’s clock and the homebody’s clock, arising and increasing on the way “out,” decreases on the way back and disappears completely at the moment the twins meet. The logical error that led to the paradox, as we can see, consisted in ignoring the vector of motion and taking into account only the magnitude of velocity. Unfortunately, negative time flowing backward (from the future into the past) is still far from being recognized by all researchers. This happens because, at ordinary subluminal velocities, the time of a moving object is “compressed,” but always remains the familiar, positive time. At the speed of light, an object sets out and reaches its goal synchronously. Its time is “zeroed out.” The traveler is as though “multiplied,” being in several places at once, that is, acquiring the properties of a wave. Superluminal objects, however, are constantly in negative time, since they always outrun the light wave with which they initially stood “on the same starting line.” In principle, they cannot be visually monitored and make themselves known only through indirect signs.

pages.title: A TALE OF LOST TIME — Schrödinger’s Cat
pages.text: Photons need some time to reach an observer; that is, every emission of particles takes place before it is detected. Thus, the movement of photons (and indeed any movement) from an “event” toward an observer occurs in ordinary positive time — from the past into the present (future), that is, with an increase in the magnitude of positive time values or a decrease in negative ones. Movement away from the observer, on the contrary, occurs in “reverse” time, from the future into the past. Reverse movement through time can occur either with a decrease in the magnitude of positive numbers or with an increase in the magnitude of negative numbers, depending on the chosen coordinate value of the starting point. The speed of movement is only of secondary importance, in the sense that the decrease or increase in the absolute values of time occurs faster at a higher speed. The subluminal speed of an observed object, with a negative increment in magnitude, makes it possible to register only the contraction or slowing of time. At the speed of light (characteristic of energy-carrying particles), the negative increment “cancels out” the entire passage of positive time. Superluminal objects always exist in minus time, that is, in genuinely negative time. In negative time, antiparticles live invisibly. Researchers studying antihydrogen have reminded us of this once again. Objects consisting of large quantities of antimatter are what is known as “dark matter”. Negative time means superluminal speeds. Ordinary objects and those composed of antimatter are separated from one another solely by the barrier of speed. This “antiworld” is visually unobservable to us, but it affects objects in the visible, “material” world, up to the point of annihilation with it at the moment of the Big Bang, which begins a new cycle in the formation of worlds that are opposites of one another, ad infinitum.
